newsitem.title: RUSSIA: PRESS DIGEST - IZVESTIA - RUSSIA - JUNE 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IZVESTIA - RUSSIA - JUNE 4.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the June 5 edition of Russia's Izvestia newspaper. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Russian budget is being crippled by the burden of the army of state officials it has to cater for.
- A televised statement by the head of Russia's security service inviting those spying for foreign countries in Russia to become double agents has turned out to be no joke.
- Pyotr Karpov, deputy head of the state agency on bankruptcies, under investigation on alleged graft charges, has been released from jail, pending trial.
- Moscow city bonds have been given a warm reception on the world market.
- Russia is no longer on the verge of bankruptcy but will remain a debtor nation for at least 25 years.
- A museum of the history of accountancy is to open in Moscow shortly.
